Name: Matt Loomis
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that my honors students can read and understand social studies articles that are written at an adult level. I have since given them much higher level text passages to read. Engaging in this process has led me to find more ways to include non-print texts in my lessons.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
One of my students used the phrase "usable past" to vividly describe how the painting of Washington and his troops crossing the Delaware River has been used to shape American cultural identify. It demonstrates how much my students are capable of with careful instructional planning and support.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? While looking at the early drafts, I am noticing that students are capable of exceptional work, but they also often make very significant mistakes in sentence structure and grammar.
